recommendations: Treat a vat-photopolymer humidity-driven bilayer as plausibly novel but run a patent and Scopus/Web of Science check before claiming it; the nearest prior art is DLP bilayers that bend on water immersion (Zhao 2017, 2018) and PolyJet swelling parts (Raviv 2014).

Before printing, measure for each candidate resin the linear hygroscopic strain and the modulus as functions of RH. Every Timoshenko failure found here traces to using dry-state or single-point material data.

Use kappa <= 1.5*d_eps/h as the first machine-checkable law: it needs only real-number algebra (AM-GM) and immediately rules out target curvatures a resin pair cannot reach. Report Timoshenko as an upper estimate, not a prediction, for soft or large-rotation designs.
Design near the optimum n = 1/m^2 where the bound is attained, and keep the active layer thin: fetched data run from 30 min below 1 mm to 24 h near 5 mm and ~400 h at 15-30 mm.

Benchmark the proof of concept against Cheng 2024 (15.5 m^-1 at 80% RH, 30 min, 170 cycles) and Rueggeberg & Burgert 2015 (8.7 m^-1, 24 h), and report cycles survived and a blocking force or moment, which most printed-hygromorph papers omit.
Have a second agent or a library login pull the paywalled numbers (Gladman 2016, Correa 2015, Le Duigou 2016, Holstov 2015) before the paper cites them quantitatively.
could_not_find: Any SLA/DLP (vat photopolymer) bilayer actuated by ambient relative humidity; only liquid-immersion DLP precedents were found.
Any SLS / powder-bed hygromorphic actuator; only a magnetic SLS gripper and reports of unwanted humidity swelling in SLS nylon-12.
Any hygromorph or bilayer design constrained by a proof-assistant-verified law.
Measured numbers from Gladman et al. 2016 (swelling strains, moduli, curvature): paywalled; only the abstract was read.

Measured numbers from Correa et al. 2015 (MIT DSpace returned HTTP 429), Le Duigou et al. 2016 (HAL blocked the fetch), Holstov et al. 2015 (repository 403), Reichert et al. 2015, Wood et al. 2018, Vailati et al. 2018, Erb et al. 2013.
Original Dawson et al. 1997 values for pine cone layer moduli; expansion coefficients are quoted second-hand and their units are ambiguous.
Timoshenko's 1925 text itself; the formula was taken as reproduced in three fetched open-access papers, which agree with each other.
A directly measured blocking force or blocking moment for an engineered wood or FFF bilayer; forces found are for pine cone scales (retention percentages only) and seed awns (mN, uN m).
Cycle counts beyond 170 for any printed hygromorph, and any failure-cycle (fatigue limit) figure.
Wheat awn and chiral seed pod numbers: only abstracts were read, which carry none.
The Urbach Tower panel curvature radius and lamella thickness.
A single agreed exponent for response time versus thickness; Reyssat & Mahadevan measured 1.3-1.5 for pine cone tissue, below the diffusive value of 2.

specialists.topic: Patents and prior art around law-constrained, printed stimulus-responsive architectural materials (preliminary scan, not legal advice)
specialists.summary: PRELIMINARY SCAN, NOT LEGAL ADVICE, NOT A FREEDOM-TO-OPERATE OR PATENTABILITY OPINION. Run 2026-11-12 with keyword searches on Google Patents (one batch of 18 queries before the service returned HTTP 503 for the rest of the run) and USPTO Patent Public Search (36 queries, US grants and published applications only, claims read for 22 documents). No Espacenet, WIPO, CNIPA or classification-code (CPC) search was possible, so non-US families are listed from Google Patents result rows only and their claims were not read. No patent in the user's repo or name was looked for or found: 'license your patent' presumes a filing that this scan cannot confirm exists. What looks crowded: (1) stimulus-responsive printed objects in general - MIT/Stratasys hold a granted method patent (US 11155025 B2, 2013 priority) on multi-material printing with differential swelling arranged into joints giving a predicted shape transformation, and the 2015 parent application claimed any additively manufactured object that transforms predictably under a non-biasing stimulus; (2) hydrogel-composite 4D printing with anisotropic fillers (Harvard applications 2015-2019); (3) hygromorphic material compositions and coated/printed bilayers (MIT 9931829, NTU 12655582, CMU 12575478, US Air Force 10457780, CityU application); (4) wood-bilayer self-shaping building parts and shading (ETH Zurich WO2018033422, Empa DE112019001411, University of Stuttgart EP4019251) - backed by a deep academic record from 2009-2024 that is itself prior art against any broad claim to a humidity-driven printed bilayer or a hygromorphic facade flap. The bilayer curvature mechanics have been public since 1925. What looks open in this scan: zero US documents had 'theorem prover' or 'proof assistant' in the claims together with material/geometry/mechanical and design terms; zero had formal-verification terms in claims about a design/model/build file with a certificate; zero combined biological/morphological/scaling-law constraints with a design space and additive manufacturing in the claims. The nearest formal-methods patents are in software and systems architecture (Microsoft US 8473895, theorem-prover-driven design-space exploration of architectures), chips, and cyber-physical monitors (CMU application). Kinds of thing that could plausibly be novel here, in descending order of how open the scan found them: (a) a design-and-verification METHOD - generating candidate geometries/material layouts, checking each against machine-checked biological and physical laws in a proof assistant, and releasing only candidates with a proof certificate to a printer; (b) a certified design FILE FORMAT / data structure binding geometry, material assignment and a machine-checkable proof (the '.life' idea) - open in the scan but software/data-structure claims face subject-matter eligibility hurdles, especially in the US, and need a concrete technical effect; (c) a specific GEOMETRY that the law-constrained search finds and that shows a measured, unexpected response - patentable only as the specific structure, not the bilayer principle; (d) a MATERIAL COMPOSITION - least promising if the proof of concept uses stock commercial resins, since the vendor's formulations are not ours and hygromorphic compositions are already heavily claimed. Any public dashboard, repo, preprint or paper already disclosing the method counts as prior art against a later filing in most jurisdictions (the US has a one-year grace period for the inventor's own disclosure; most others do not) - unverified background, to be confirmed with counsel before the paper is posted.

findings.claim: The 2015 MIT/Stratasys application claim 1 as published was very broad: an object comprising an additive manufacturing material configured to cause a predicted transformation from a first manufactured shape to a second in response to a non-biasing external stimulus. This is a published application claim, not the granted claim; the granted continuation is narrower (two formulations, differential swelling, joints in series).

MIT holds a granted US patent whose claim 1 covers applying hygromorphic material to one side of an object in a spatially varying distribution so that the object's humidity-driven shape change depends on that distribution and includes forming a sharply angled bend; dependent claims name hydrogel and bacterial cells.

findings.claim: Harvard filed US applications claiming 4D printing of hydrogel composite filaments with embedded anisotropic filler particles deposited in two layers of predetermined arrangement that swell on hydration into a curved 3D structure, and a variant printing onto a flexible substrate. Both were found only as published applications in this scan; grant status was not determined.

Harvard and MIT filed a US application on a printed lattice whose ribs are bilayers of filaments with different thermal expansion and/or modulus so that the lattice adopts a predetermined 3D geometry under a stimulus. Found as an application only; grant status not determined.

Nanyang Technological University holds a granted US patent on a hygromorphic composite: a moisture-active pollen-paper substrate with a moisture-inactive toner/ink layer printed in a pattern that makes the composite change shape in a predetermined way with relative humidity.

Carnegie Mellon holds a granted US patent on an artificial seed carrier with a wood body that coils and uncoils with humidity to self-drill into a substrate (a seed-inspired hygromorphic device, not a building element).

findings.claim: No US document was found claiming a design/model/build file carrying a proof or certificate checked by a theorem prover, proof checker or formal verification; and none claiming biological/morphological/allometric/scaling-law constraints on a design space for an additively manufactured material or structure.

Full-text co-occurrence of theorem prover / proof assistant with additive manufacturing or 3D printing is nearly absent in US documents: 3 hits, none about material design (a robotics executive network, a vaccine method, a conversational AI system). Google Patents returned 0 for four related phrase queries before it began refusing requests.

findings.claim: The closest formal-methods patent found is Microsoft's: a computer-implemented method that symbolically executes a design specification into a quantifier-free logical formula and interacts with a theorem prover module to find distinct solutions (architectures) within a design space. It concerns system/software architectures, not physical materials, but it shows 'theorem prover + design space exploration' as a generic concept was claimed with a 2010 filing.

Other formal-methods neighbours are in cyber-physical systems and engineering architecture generation, not materials: a CMU application on synthesizing a runtime monitor from a proven hybrid model of a cyber-physical system, and a Siemens patent on a modeling language for generating engineering design architectures.

At least one 2026 individual-inventor US application family in the metamaterial area mentions proof assistants in its specification (stating the invention is not limited to any proof assistant or verification environment) while claiming a fabrication process, not a verification method. This shows proof-assistant language is starting to appear in materials filings.

Computational design-method claims for shape-morphing structures exist but are specific: Toyota holds a granted patent on designing and additively manufacturing an inflatable shape-morphing structure via finite-element topology optimization converted to a Turing-pattern texture. A claims-field query for stimulus-driven shape change + simulation/optimization/inverse design + 3D printing + target shape returned zero US documents.

No US document was found claiming vat-photopolymerization / stereolithography / DLP printing combined with shape change or shape memory, a water/humidity/swelling trigger and a bilayer/gradient/grayscale architecture. The resin-printer route to a hygromorphic part therefore looked uncrowded by keyword, but a separate query showed Toyota/Georgia Tech hold a 2023-priority patent on grayscale DLP printed shape-morphing (US 12768208 B2), whose claims were not read.
findings.value: numFound=0 (query s_resin_sla); US 12768208 B2 listed under query p_selfshape

findings.claim: The physics of the bilayer is long-public: the curvature of a two-layer strip under differential expansion was derived in 1925, applied to pine-cone-like hygromorphs in 2009, demonstrated in 3D-printed wood composites in 2015, in hydrogel 4D printing in 2016, at building scale in wood in 2018-2019, and as 4D-printed cellulose weather-responsive shading on a real facade in 2024. Any claim reading on a humidity-driven printed bilayer flap as such would meet this literature.
findings.source_url_or_path: https://api.crossref.org/works (each DOI resolved in this run; saved scratch/spec-ip-landscape/crossref.json)

findings.claim: Inverse design of shape-shifting bilayers (computing the growth pattern for a target shape) is published academic prior art (2017) and was reduced to practice in printed lattices (2019), so 'compute the print pattern that yields a target shape' is not new as a concept.

Using the Lean theorem prover to formalize physical-science derivations is published (chemical physics, 2024; high-energy physics, 2024 preprint), and a 2026 preprint applies Lean 4 with machine-checkable certificates to patent analysis itself. None of the three describes constraining a printable material or geometry design space. So 'formalize science in Lean' is not new; applying machine-checked laws as a gate on fabricable designs was not found.

Formlabs' own US filings returned by a keyword query for shape memory / swelling / shape change / hygroscopic / 4D were about mixing, casting molds, support structures and dentures, not stimulus-responsive printed parts. Only the first 14 of 37 family-expanded results were inspected.

Coverage limits of this scan: Google Patents answered 18 queries then returned HTTP 503 for 22 further queries and all single-patent pages; Espacenet, WIPO Patentscope, Justia and uspto.report returned 403. The remaining 36 queries ran on USPTO Patent Public Search, which covers US grants and published applications only. No CPC-class search, no citation chaining, no legal-status or assignment check, no non-English full text.
findings.value: 18 Google Patents queries answered, 22 refused; 13+15+8=36 USPTO queries; 22 US documents with claims read

recommendations: Treat this as a first-pass keyword scan only. Before anyone tells an investor there is something to license, establish whether any patent application has actually been filed by the team; this scan found none and did not look inside the team's own records.

Before the paper, dashboard or repo discloses the law-constrained design pipeline publicly, ask a patent attorney whether to file a provisional. Public disclosure is prior art against later filings in most jurisdictions (unverified background on grace periods: confirm with counsel). Check what is already public on the live dashboard and in the repo history.

Frame the candidate invention as a design-and-verification method (machine-checked biological/physical law set as a gate on generated geometries, with a proof certificate released to the printer) rather than as a humidity bilayer. The bilayer principle, hygromorphic compositions and 4D printing as such are crowded; the method and a certified design file were the only areas with zero keyword hits.

If a certified file format ('.life') is pursued, tie claims to a concrete technical effect (for example, a printer or slicer that refuses to build without a valid proof, or a measured property guaranteed by the certified constraint), since bare data structures and abstract verification steps face eligibility objections. This is a question for counsel.

Commission a professional search before relying on the open-space finding: CPC classes B33Y, B29C64, E04F10 / E06B9 (shading), G06F30 (computer-aided design) and G06N5 (knowledge-based reasoning), plus Espacenet and CNIPA full text. Chinese 4D-printing filings were visible in results but not analysed.

Read the claims of the three building-scale wood-bilayer families (ETH WO2018033422, Empa DE112019001411, Stuttgart EP4019251) and of MIT/Stratasys US 11155025 before the proof-of-concept is described commercially; these are the families a printed hygromorphic architectural element is most likely to sit next to.

Do not plan on a material-composition claim if the demonstration uses unmodified commercial resins. A specific geometry found by the constrained search, with a measured unexpected response, is the more defensible physical claim.
Keep a dated record of which Lean laws constrained which design and what the measured print did; whichever route is taken, that record is the evidence of conception and of the technical effect.

specialists.topic: Levin lab: xenobots, bioelectricity, and an optogenetic, hands-off variant (label spec-levin-bioelectric)
specialists.summary: Three generations of Xenopus biobot are measurable from fetched sources: gen-1 cardiomyocyte-driven designs evolved in a voxel soft-body simulator (Kriegman 2020, PNAS), gen-2 cilia-driven spheroids of 3026 +/- 180 cells at 487-602 um diameter moving at >100 um/s and living 9-10 d unfed or >90 d in media (Blackiston 2021, Sci Robot), and kinematically self-replicating semitoroids reaching 3 +/- 0.8 replication rounds vs 1.2 +/- 0.4 for spheroids (Kriegman 2021, PNAS). Anthrobots from a single adult human lung cell are 30-500 um and move at 5-50 um/s (Gumuskaya 2024, Adv Sci). The decisive finding for the brief is Fotowat et al. 2026 (Adv Sci, Levin lab): 'neurobots' built from Xenopus ectoderm plus implanted neural precursors show enrichment of visual-perception pathways exclusively in neurobots, including rhodopsin (rho), cone opsins (opn1lw, opn1sw), melanopsin (opn4, opn5) and rgr, and the authors state the neurobots 'could potentially sense and process light stimuli' -- inferred from transcriptome only, with NO light-response behaviour tested and optogenetic activation named explicitly as future work. So the brief's 'optogenetic xenobot where light sensors trigger movements' is, as of today, an open and publicly flagged gap, not a published result. The one reported instance of light-driven xenobot locomotion (ChR2 by mRNA microinjection, significant velocity increase, paired t-test p=0.0124, n=8) exists only in a Levin/Blackiston patent that I could not fetch directly, and in no peer-reviewed paper: a Europe PMC query for (xenobot OR 'biological robot' OR anthrobot) AND (optogenetic OR channelrhodopsin) returns 8 hits, none of them such a study. Peer-reviewed precedent for light-driven biohybrid locomotion is in other systems: ChR2 cardiomyocytes steering a 1/10-scale soft-robotic ray by light frequency and independent left/right fin stimulation (Park 2016, Science), optogenetic skeletal muscle giving up to 300 uN (0.56 kPa) and 310 um/s locomotion (Raman 2016, PNAS), and bPAC raising cAMP to accelerate flagellar beat within seconds (Jansen 2015, eLife) -- which makes bPAC, not a cation channel, the mechanistically better-supported effector for a cilia-driven bot, since ciliary beat frequency is cAMP-dependent. On the local .life format: it is a genuinely strong provenance and consistency layer (five per-cell channels, per-channel provenance stamps, five refusals, a measured/assumed/depicted/not-established value vocabulary, usableFor gating, stamped STL and FASTA export) and it cannot currently express this experiment at all. A grep of the whole organism-format tree for opsin|light|optogen|locomot|behaviour|actuat|cilia|contract|velocity|motil returns zero vocabulary hits -- the only matches are prose in comments and one scope string. There is no locomotion channel, no stimulus/actuation axis, no membrane-potential channel, no sub-ontogenetic time unit (all eight TIME_UNITS are developmental, none are seconds), and no causal link from a genome edit to a behaviour, so 'genome to locomotion' would be two unlinked records in one file. Computationally, the morphology-and-motion half is validatable today with open tools (Voxelyze/VoxCAD, CompuCell3D, Morpheus, PhysiCell, BETSE for bioelectrics); the chain opsin photocurrent -> ciliary beat frequency -> hydrodynamic thrust has no open published implementation I could find, and that is the real computational gap. On nonprofits: the only clearly confirmed one is The Guy Foundation Family Trust, a registered charity in England and Wales (no. 1178782), which granted US$199,589 and US$290,778 to Levin's Tufts lab for bioelectric-field work; ICDO's legal status is stated nowhere I could fetch, and Morphoceuticals, Fauna Systems and Astonishing Labs are companies.

findings.claim: Gen-2 cilia-driven xenobots are spheres of 3026 +/- 180 cells that differentiate into ciliated epithelium over 4 days
findings.value: 3026 +/- 180 cells; ciliated epithelium by day 4; motile from day 3

findings.claim: Fully differentiated xenobot spheres range from 487 +/- 39 um (smallest cut explants, n=15) to 602 +/- 30 um (largest, n=13) in diameter
Xenobots move at rates exceeding 100 um/s in aqueous solution
findings.value: >100 um/s (the published PDF text reads '100 m/s'; the micro sign is lost in pdftotext extraction, and 100 m/s is physically impossible for a 0.5 mm swimmer)

findings.claim: Normalised xenobot speed is about 0.18 body lengths per second
findings.value: 100 um/s / ((487+602)/2 = 544.5 um) = 0.18 BL/s -- my own calculation from the two Blackiston figures

findings.claim: Xenobots are self-powered on maternal yolk platelets for 9-10 days, extendable beyond 90 days in Xenopus-specific culture media
findings.value: 9-10 d unfed; >90 d in culture media

findings.claim: Xenobot average velocity does not change significantly across the lifespan, but doubling body size significantly reduces it
findings.value: lifespan effect Kruskal-Wallis P = 0.29; size doubling Student t test P = 0.04, attributed to reduced surface-to-volume ratio

findings.claim: Xenobots locomoted through confined spaces down to a 580 um inner-diameter capillary

Blackiston 2021 already demonstrates a hands-off, imaging-free light experiment: xenobots expressing photoconvertible EosFP were released into a 5 cm arena with a 7 mm illuminated spot 20 mm from the loading zone, left 1 hour unsupervised, then scored after the fact; 3 of 10 showed strong red emission
findings.value: 5 cm arena; 7 mm spot; 20 mm away; 1 h; 390-400 nm light; 10 individuals released, 3 strongly photoconverted

findings.claim: Cilia-driven locomotion is abolished by overexpressing the Notch receptor intracellular domain (NotchICD), which diverts differentiating tissue to other epidermal fates -- a clean genetic negative control for any light-driven-motility claim
findings.value: NotchICD overexpression; multiciliated cells quantified per 500 um diameter region

findings.claim: Gen-1 (cardiomyocyte) xenobot papers report no absolute body length; a 100 um concavity is described as 12% of total body length, implying roughly 833 um
findings.value: 100 um / 0.12 = 833 um (my calculation). Contraction cycled at 2 Hz; selection on net displacement over a 10 s period; 6 organisms built; ground contact 52.7% then 93.3% of the gait cycle

findings.claim: Gen-1 xenobots were built from pluripotent blastula cells, epidermal cells and cardiac progenitors, reared at 14 C, with 370 pg mRNA microinjected per transcript into all four cells
findings.value: 14 C rearing; 22 C healing; 20 C imaging; 370 pg mRNA per transcript; 5 animal caps pooled per construct; designs >50% muscle were filtered out

findings.claim: Kinematic self-replication: semitoroid progenitors achieved 3 +/- 0.8 replication rounds (max 4) versus 1.2 +/- 0.4 (max 2) for spheroids, a 250% increase
findings.value: 3 +/- 0.8 SD vs 1.2 +/- 0.4 SD rounds; +250%, P < 0.05; offspring diameter 149% larger, Mann-Whitney P = 0.037; generations P = 0.019; size-generation correlation rho = 0.93

findings.claim: Self-replication required ~60,000 dissociated stem cells in a 60 mm dish at 25-150 cells/mm2, with a minimum pile of at least 50 cells to mature into an offspring; one replication round takes about a week and wild-type organisms live 10-14 days
findings.value: ~60,000 cells per 60 mm dish; 25-150 cells/mm2; >=50 cells minimum pile; ~3,000 cells per progenitor; 1 week per round; 20 h per trial generation; lifespan 10-14 d; 14 C culture, 20 C trials

findings.claim: The self-replication design search used a GPU-parallelised voxel-based soft-body simulator (unnamed in text, cited to ref. 40) with a pile threshold of 108 voxels, 9 progenitors and 1,262 simulated loose cells per dish, 49 independent trials, 48 h wall clock on eight NVIDIA Tesla V100s, integration step 2.14e-4 s over 16,366 steps
findings.value: 108 voxels threshold; 9 progenitors + 1,262 cells; 49 trials; 48 h on 8x V100; 2.14e-4 s step; 16,366 steps; 3.5 s evaluation

findings.claim: Anthrobots are 30-500 um in diameter, form from a single adult human lung cell after about two weeks in extracellular matrix, move by cilia at 5-50 um/s, and can traverse and rapidly repair scratches in cultured human neural sheets
findings.value: 30-500 um diameter; 5-50 um/s; single seed cell; ~2 weeks in ECM. Normalised: 50 um/s / 300 um = 0.17 BL/s (my calculation)

findings.claim: DECISIVE GAP: Levin-lab 'neurobots' (2026) show enrichment of visual-perception pathways exclusively in neurobots, including rhodopsin (rho), cone opsins opn1lw and opn1sw, melanopsin opn4 and opn5, and rgr; the authors state the neurobots 'could potentially sense and process light stimuli' but tested NO light-response behaviour and name optogenetic activation of neurons only as future work
findings.value: opsin genes rho, opn1lw, opn1sw, opn4, opn5, rgr; retinal development genes neurod1, neurod2, pou4f1, onecut1, lhx1, unc5d, prdm13; 6,774 genes up / 3,578 down vs biobots; inference from transcriptome only

findings.claim: Neurobots are significantly larger than non-neural biobots, show more complex movement, differ in response to neuroactive drugs, and have the same 9-10 day unfed lifespan; neural precursors came from animal caps of about 50 embryos
findings.value: size Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.0007; n = 46 neurobots vs 48 biobots in movement recordings; 16 vs 16 in the PTZ experiment at 15 mM PTZ; calcium imaging 10 min at 5 frames/s; neurite extremes 327 terminals / 7635.9 mm vs 40 terminals / 753.8 mm; lifespan ~9-10 d unfed; ~50 embryos' animal caps per precursor pool

findings.claim: No peer-reviewed study of optogenetic or channelrhodopsin control of xenobots, biobots or anthrobots exists in Europe PMC
findings.value: Europe PMC query (xenobot OR 'biological robot' OR anthrobot) AND (optogenetic OR channelrhodopsin) returns 8 total hits, all reviews or unrelated platform papers (e.g. Drosophila microrobotics 10.1073/pnas.2426180122, biohybrid review 10.1038/s44182-025-00056-x); none reports light-driven biobot locomotion

findings.claim: The only reported light-driven xenobot locomotion is in a Levin/Blackiston patent, not in the literature: ChR2 delivered by mRNA microinjection gave a significant velocity increase under blue light versus untreated controls, and the filing claims to be first to show control of cilia beating with light
findings.value: paired t-test p = 0.0124, n = 8 individuals per treatment; ChR2 by mRNA microinjection; proposed mechanism is cation efflux raising cilia beat frequency. Patent US20220220437A1 / granted US12215344, 'Engineered multicellular ciliated organisms and kinematic self-replication thereof'
findings.source_url_or_path: WebSearch extract of https://patents.google.com/patent/US20220220437A1/en -- I could NOT fetch the patent document itself: patents.google.com returned HTTP 503 on three attempts, the USPTO PDF exceeded the 10 MB fetch limit and a curl of it truncated at 3.8 MB with an unreadable xref table, patentguru returned 468, espacenet 403, freepatentsonline ECONNRESET

findings.claim: Peer-reviewed precedent for light-steered biohybrid locomotion: a 1/10-scale soft-robotic ray with optogenetically engineered rat cardiomyocytes on a microfabricated gold skeleton, where light frequency sets speed and independent left/right fin stimulation sets direction through an obstacle course
findings.value: 1/10 scale; serpentine muscle circuits; sequential light-triggered activation. Absolute length, mass, cardiomyocyte count, wavelength and irradiance were NOT in the records I fetched (PMC5526330 fullTextXML returned HTTP 500)

findings.claim: Optogenetic skeletal-muscle bioactuators on 3D-printed flexible skeletons reach up to 300 uN (0.56 kPa) active tension under non-invasive optical stimulation, driving 310 um/s directional locomotion (1.3 body lengths/min) and 2 deg/s steering, and adapt after exercise training
findings.value: 300 uN (0.56 kPa); 310 um/s = 1.3 BL/min; 2 deg/s rotation

findings.claim: bPAC (photoactivated adenylyl cyclase) is the mechanistically better-supported effector for a cilia-driven bot than a cation channel, because light-triggered cAMP elevation accelerates the flagellar beat within seconds and restored motility and in vitro fertilisation in sperm lacking bicarbonate-stimulated sACY
findings.value: beat frequency rises within seconds of light; restored IVF in sACY-null sperm

findings.claim: Direct ciliary targeting of optogenetic tools can impair protein function, so fusing bPAC or LAPD to cilia-localising sequences reduces activity -- a design constraint for any cilia-targeted opsin
findings.source_url_or_path: https://www.zfin.org/ZDB-FIG-200715-7 (reported in a WebSearch result; I did not fetch the underlying paper, so treat as a flag to check rather than a settled constraint)

findings.claim: Light-gated ion translocators have already been used in Xenopus by the Levin lab to control bioelectric state and tumorigenesis, and optogenetics has been used in Xenopus to prevent ethanol-induced brain and eye defects -- so the opsin-in-Xenopus half of the design is established, independent of biobots

findings.claim: I could not find any published light dose for driving xenobot motility: no irradiance in mW/mm2 appears in any xenobot source I fetched. The only xenobot light numbers are 390-400 nm for photoconverting the EosFP recorder, which is a readout, not an actuator

recommendations: Build the optogenetic design on the one hands-off experiment that is already published rather than on the patent. Blackiston 2021 released 10 EosFP-expressing xenobots into a 5 cm arena with a 7 mm illuminated spot 20 mm away, left them 1 hour with no imaging and no handling, and scored photoconversion afterwards; 3 of 10 had been exposed. Pair that integrator with a light-driven actuator and you get open-loop drive plus a post-hoc record with zero live microscopy -- exactly the 'no imaging or direct interaction' constraint in the brief, and it is defensible from a fetched source.

Choose bPAC over ChR2 as the effector, and say why in the paper. Ciliary and flagellar beat frequency is cAMP-dependent, and bPAC's light-to-cAMP-to-faster-beat chain is peer-reviewed with a seconds-scale latency (Jansen 2015, eLife 10.7554/eLife.05161). The ChR2 route for ciliated biobots rests on a cation-efflux mechanism the patent itself only calls 'hypothesised', and it is unpublished. A reviewer will ask which link in the chain is measured; with bPAC the answer is the effector link.

Use the published negative control. NotchICD overexpression diverts the differentiating tissue to non-ciliated epidermal fates and abolishes motion (Blackiston 2021). A light-driven-motility claim with a NotchICD arm distinguishes 'light raised the beat frequency' from 'light did something else that happened to move the bot'. Without it the velocity change is uninterpretable, which is the main weakness of the n=8, p=0.0124 patent result.

Deliver the opsin by mRNA microinjection at the 4-cell stage, not as a transgene. Kriegman 2020 injected 370 pg of mRNA per transcript into all four cells; Blackiston used the same route for NotchICD, EosFP, centrin-RFP and CLAMP-GFP. This keeps the genome reference-only, which means the .life genome block stays an honest edit-free record and the FASTA export correctly refuses rather than emitting a reference assembly dressed up as a design.

Treat the light dose as an open hole and pre-register it as not-established. No irradiance in mW/mm2 for driving xenobot motility appears in any source I could fetch; the only xenobot light numbers are 390-400 nm for photoconverting a recorder. Put it in the .organism as a not-established entry with a what_would_resolve_it field naming the measurement (irradiance at the arena floor, exposure duration, and the resulting velocity, with a NotchICD arm) -- the format is built for exactly this and it is more credible than importing a number from a patent.

Lead the paper with the 2026 neurobot gap, because it is the strongest framing available and it is Levin's own. Fotowat et al. (10.1002/advs.202508967) found rho, opn1lw, opn1sw, opn4, opn5 and rgr enriched exclusively in neurobots and wrote that these bots 'could potentially sense and process light stimuli', tested no light behaviour, and named optogenetic activation as future work. A 'light sensors trigger movements' design is therefore the published next step of the field's own paper, not a speculative pivot. Note the albino caveat: the calcium-imaging bots were albino and the authors flag that albino tadpoles differ in visually evoked behaviour.

Extend .life with four things before claiming it can hold a genome-to-locomotion design, and keep the format's own discipline while doing it: (1) a behaviour channel carrying the four quantities Blackiston actually computed -- position, linear speed, heading, angular speed -- with a provenance stamp per track, not per point; (2) a stimulus block with wavelength_nm, irradiance_mW_per_mm2, duty_cycle, exposure_s and a geometry for where the light was; (3) a seconds-scale time unit, which forces a decision about no_cross_unit_distance rather than silently violating it; (4) a membrane_potential channel with readout_kind and is_relative, mirroring the mechanics channel's hard-won lesson that a field name must not impose a unit the measurement does not have.

Add one refusal rather than one field for the causal claim: no_unlinked_mechanism -- a file that carries both a genome edit and a behaviour measurement, and no stated mechanism connecting them, degrades rather than passes. This is the same move the format already makes with no_identity_drift, and it is the difference between a genome-to-locomotion file and two records in one envelope. 'Nothing checked is not a pass' is already a standing rule in the spec; this applies it to the claim the whole project rests on.

Scope the computational validation honestly in the paper: the morphology-and-motion half is validatable today in open tools (Voxelyze for soft-body actuation and thrust, CompuCell3D or Morpheus or PhysiCell for the morphogenesis, BETSE for the bioelectric state), but no open simulator couples a photocurrent to a ciliary beat frequency to a thrust. In Blackiston 2021 the cilia force is a manually tuned tangential force per surface voxel. Writing that coupling -- even a one-parameter map from irradiance to per-voxel tangential force, calibrated against one measured velocity -- is a small, publishable, and genuinely missing piece.

Do not let an STL exported from a .life reach a printer or a solver unexamined. Binary STL has no unit field, most slicers assume millimetres, and a 500 um bot is then wrong by 1000x; separately, the sphere-packing shape model has no contact faces, so exposed surface area is overestimated in exactly the direction that inflates the ciliated area a thrust estimate depends on. Both are stated in the format's own README; the thrust bias should be written into any simulation result as a derived value with its rule named.

For funding and framing, The Guy Foundation Family Trust (charity no. 1178782) is the one confirmed nonprofit funder with a track record here -- two grants to Levin's Tufts lab totalling about US$490k for bioelectric-field and V-ATPase work. ICDO is the natural institutional partner for a computationally designed organism, but its legal status is stated nowhere public, so ask directly rather than describing it as a nonprofit in any document.

Avoid one trap in the measured numbers: the Blackiston PDF's '100 m/s' is a lost micro sign and the self-replication paper gives NO absolute parent or offspring diameters in um, only scale bars and percentage changes (+149%). Any table that prints a self-replication diameter in microns is inventing it. Likewise the 30-500 um anthrobot range is confirmed in the published abstract but no cell count per anthrobot was in anything I fetched.

Any peer-reviewed paper on optogenetic or channelrhodopsin control of xenobot, biobot or anthrobot locomotion. A Europe PMC query returned 8 hits, none of them such a study. This looks like a real hole in the literature rather than a search failure, and it is the hole the brief proposes to fill.

A light dose for driving biobot motility. No irradiance in mW/mm2, and no actuation wavelength, appears in any xenobot or anthrobot source I fetched. The only xenobot light figures are 390 nm and 400 nm for photoconverting the EosFP recorder.

Absolute parent and offspring diameters in um for the self-replicating xenobots. The paper reports only scale bars and percentage differences (offspring +149%). Any micron figure for these would be invented.
Cell count per anthrobot. The published abstract gives diameter and speed but no cell number, and I did not reach the full text.

The name of the simulator used in either xenobot design paper. Kriegman 2020 calls it 'a physics engine' in the main text and defers to SI S3; Kriegman 2021 says 'a GPU-parallelized version of a voxel-based soft-body simulator' citing ref. 40 without naming it. Any open simulator that couples an opsin photocurrent to ciliary beat frequency to hydrodynamic thrust. I found none. BETSE covers bioelectrics, Voxelyze covers soft-body actuation as an abstract force, and nothing bridges them.
ICDO's legal or tax status. Its own site, Levin's resources page and the search results all state nothing about nonprofit registration, incorporation or funding.
The Allen Discovery Center at Tufts award amount. The Allen Institute announcement URL returned HTTP 404.

Peer-reviewed confirmation that direct ciliary targeting impairs optogenetic tool function. specialists.topic: Deep read: Marom, Tibbits, Zardini and Buehler 2026 (JMPS, arXiv:2604.26367) and Marom and Buehler 2025 (MRS Bulletin); code repo lamm-mit/CategoryTheoryDesign; overlap with ThompsonLaws/Hygromorphs.lean
specialists.summary: The task brief assumed the paper treats pine cone scales, wheat awns, seed pods and the Venus flytrap each with its own equation and parameters. It does not. The paper (arXiv:2604.26367v2; J. Mech. Phys. Solids 216, 106780, doi:10.1016/j.jmps.2026.106780) instantiates ONE biological system, the pine cone scale, as a five-object chain (fiber, lamina, tissue, element, organ). Wheat awns, chiral seed pods, the flytrap and nacre appear only as one-sentence motivating examples with no equations or parameters. The category Dyn has objects (X, E, f) with dynamics x' = f(x,e) and morphisms (alpha, alpha_E) of smooth maps satisfying the simulation condition d(alpha)_x(f(x,e)) = g(alpha(x), alpha_E(e)); 'preserve dynamics' means exactly that. Proved on paper: Dyn is a category (chain rule), Nat/Art are full subcategories, a reduction compatible with the dynamics induces a unique quotient dynamics, alpha_geom and alpha_3 are morphisms, Spec and Comp are categories, and F, pi, E are functors. Most of these proofs are definitional (pi sends every Spec morphism to an identity because Spec morphisms are DEFINED as projection-preserving; F is conjugation by chosen diffeomorphisms that are identities in every example). The paper itself says verification is 'a claim about composition, not about any single model'; model fidelity is left to experiment. Physical work WAS done: four FFF bilayer strips (100 x 10 mm, 0.6 + 0.6 mm) printed on a Bambu Lab X1 Carbon from pipeline-generated G-code, equilibrium angles measured, n = 3 or 4 per case: 35.3 +/- 3.1 deg vs 36.4 predicted (hygro bend), 55.7 +/- 4.2 vs 52.0 (thermal bend), 41.3 +/- 2.2 vs 41.3 (hygro twist), 23.3 +/- 2.5 vs 23.0 (thermal twist). No parameter values appear in the paper text; they live in the repo's Grasshopper panels, which I extracted (table below). The paper has no dynamics data (no relaxation times given or measured), no uncertainty propagation, single-object-per-scale only. Hygromorphs.lean already machine-checks the Dyn category (in a normed-space, merely-differentiable version), composition closure, solution-mapping, the Timoshenko coefficient (including a derivation from beam equilibrium the paper only cites), the cos^2/sin^2 strain projection, the shear formula and the same-material antisymmetric mismatch (eq 28). It does NOT check Nat/Art, the reduction proposition, alpha_1/alpha_2/alpha_geom/alpha_3 as morphisms, the functor F, the natural transformation eta, Spec/Comp/pi/E, the fiber relaxation law, theta = L kappa, the thermal variant, or any number. The Lean file's flytrap snap parameter, diffusive h^2/D time and poroelastic time are NOT from this paper. A finding of my own from the repo code: the printed twist specimens use two DIFFERENT materials at +/-45 deg, so eq 28 (and Lean's shearStrain_mismatch / axialStrain_mismatch = 0) does not strictly apply; the repo's own formulas give a non-zero bending 'crosstalk' the paper does not discuss. I could reproduce only one of the four predicted angles (hygro twist, 41.33 deg) from the repo panels; the other three do not follow from a single stimulus setting I could identify.

findings.claim: Bibliographic identity: 'A Category-Theoretic Framework from Biological Mechanics to Engineered Stimulus-Response Systems', Lee Marom, Skylar Tibbits, Gioele Zardini, Markus J. Buehler. arXiv v1 2026-04-29, v2 2026-08-20; categories cond-mat.soft (primary), cond-mat.mtrl-sci, cs.CE, math.CT. Journal version: J. Mech. Phys. Solids vol 216, article 106780, issued 2026-10, doi:10.1016/j.jmps.2026.106780.

Object of Dyn: a triple S = (X, E, f); X a smooth finite-dimensional state manifold, E a smooth finite-dimensional stimulus manifold, f : X x E -> TX smooth with f(x,e) in T_x X; dynamics x' = f(x,e) (eqs 2-3, A.6-A.8).

Morphism of Dyn: a pair of smooth maps (alpha : X -> Y, alpha_E : E -> F) satisfying the simulation condition d(alpha)_x(f(x,e)) = g(alpha(x), alpha_E(e)) for all (x,e) (eq 4 / A.11). 'Preserve dynamics' is this condition: evolving at the fine scale then mapping equals mapping then evolving at the coarse scale. Identity = (id_X, id_E); composition is component-wise.

Two roles for morphisms: assembly morphisms alpha (aggregate fine-scale subsystems) and reduction morphisms beta (extract observables). The paper concedes that several betas shown in figures (individual strain components, curvature, mean opening angle) are 'terminal observables' or coordinate readouts that 'need not, by themselves, carry enough state to define closed dynamics', i.e. they are not all genuine Dyn morphisms.

Nat and Art are defined informally as the full subcategories of Dyn whose objects 'arise from natural or biological mechanisms' / 'are realized as engineered or fabricated systems'. Membership is a label, not a mathematical predicate.

Only ONE biological system is formalized: the hygromorphic pine cone, as five objects F_fib -> L_lam -> T_tis -> S_elem -> O_org linked by alpha_1 (average N fibers), alpha_2 (stack M laminae), alpha_geom (apply geometry, Timoshenko), alpha_3 (clamp K elements). Wheat awns, the Venus flytrap and nacre are each mentioned in one sentence in Sec. 1 and Sec. 3 ('Each of these can be represented as a chain of objects in Nat') with no equation or parameter; chiral seed pods are cited once (Armon 2011) as motivation for the twist case.

Fiber scale: state (m, eps_L, eps_T) in R^3, stimulus u = relative humidity; law is first-order relaxation: m' = -(m - m_eq(u))/tau_m, eps_L' = -(eps_L - chi_L (m - m0))/tau_L, eps_T' = -(eps_T - chi_T (m - m0))/tau_T (eq 6). NO numerical values for tau_m, tau_L, tau_T, chi_L, chi_T, m0 or m_eq(u) are given anywhere in the paper.

Lamina scale: alpha_1 is the arithmetic mean of N fiber states (eq 8); f_lam has the same relaxation form (eq 9). Only the uniform case (all fibers same parameters and orientation) is treated; heterogeneous fibers are deferred to a presheaf formulation in future work.

Tissue scale: X_tis = X_lam^M, laminae evolve independently (eq 12). Effective strain along the tissue axis eps = eps_L cos^2(phi) + eps_T sin^2(phi) (eq 13). For M = 2 the reduction beta_thk gives Delta_eps_thk = eps_1 - eps_2 (eq 14).

Element scale: kappa = C_geom * Delta_eps_thk (eq 15) with Timoshenko coefficient C_geom = (1/h) * 6(1+mu)^2 / (3(1+mu)^2 + (1+mu n)(mu^2 + 1/(mu n))), mu = h1/h2, n = E1/E2, h = h1+h2 (eq 16). Element state (kappa, Delta_eps_thk, m); law eq 17 with a mismatch relaxation time tau_Delta (no value given).

Organ scale: opening angle of a clamped scale of uniform curvature theta(L) = L * kappa (eq 18); organ = K independent elements; terminal observable = mean opening angle. 'No new constitutive laws are introduced at this scale.'

Implementation functor F : Nat -> Art is defined by choosing, for each object, an engineered counterpart plus diffeomorphisms iota_S, j_S that intertwine the two vector fields (A.42), and sending a morphism to its conjugate (A.44). The paper states that in all its examples iota and j 'are typically identities' so 'F reduces to parameter substitution within a fixed hierarchical schema'. Object map: fiber -> filament, lamina -> printed layer, tissue -> printed stack, element -> printed bilayer, organ -> printed object.

Caveat (my reading, not stated by the authors): A.42 requires a diffeomorphism under which the biological and engineered vector fields agree exactly. With iota = identity and different coefficients (chi, tau) the two fields are not equal, so 'parameter substitution' is not literally an instance of A.42 unless the parameters are folded into the state or iota is a rescaling. The paper does not exhibit iota for the pine cone to PA6-GF/PA612-CF case.

Spec: objects are fabrication programs Sigma = (D, P, zeta) (part domain, ordered deposition primitives, annotation map of process parameters); morphisms are annotation updates that keep D and P fixed and satisfy pi(Sigma') = pi(Sigma). pi : Spec -> Art computes effective moduli E_eff = rho * E_bulk and integer pass counts and sends every morphism to an identity. E : Spec -> Comp compiles to G-code. Comp: objects are machine programs, morphisms are semantics-preserving rewrites.
findings.source_url_or_path: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26367 (Sec. 5, App. A.6, A.7, A.10, A.11)

findings.claim: Proved by construction (paper proofs): (1) Dyn is a category, closure by chain rule; (2) Nat, Art full subcategories; (3) a reduction beta that is constant-on-fibres compatible with f induces a unique dynamics making (beta, id_E) a morphism; (4) alpha_geom is a morphism once fixed geometry is adjoined to the state with zero dynamics; (5) alpha_3 is a morphism; (6) Spec, Comp are categories; (7) F, pi, E are functors; (8) the naturality squares of eta compose (A.53). The functoriality proofs of pi and E are one-liners that follow from the definitions.

Left to experiment, in the authors' words: 'verification is a claim about composition, not about any single model... The fidelity of the models themselves, together with material variability and fabrication tolerances, remains empirical and is assessed through physical validation.'

Engineered systems: four bilayer strip actuators, shared geometry L = 100 mm, w = 10 mm, h1 = h2 = 0.6 mm. Baseline hygro bending PA6-GF (0 deg) / PA612-CF (90 deg); Case I thermal bending PLA (90 deg) / CF-PLA (0 deg); Case II hygro twisting PA6-GF (+45) / PA612-CF (-45); Case III thermal twisting PLA (+45) / CF-PLA (-45). Only the fiber object (stimulus law) and the tissue reduction (beta_thk vs beta_twist) change between cases.

Thermal variant: eigenstrain eps_L0 = alpha_L (theta - theta_0), eps_T0 = alpha_T (theta - theta_0). Twist reduction: eps_12 = (1/2)(eps_L - eps_T) sin(2 phi); antisymmetric +phi/-phi bilayer mismatch Delta_eps_12 = (eps_L - eps_T) sin(2 phi) (eq 28); thermal twist Delta_eps_12 = (alpha_L - alpha_T)(theta - theta_0) sin(2 phi) (eq 29). The paper says the twist curvature 'follows from plate theory for antisymmetric laminates' but gives no formula.

In the repo code the twist curvature is NOT a separate plate-theory expression: S_print.py computes kappa_twist = C_geom * d_12 with the same Timoshenko bending coefficient used for kappa_bend, and O_obj.py reports b_angle = degrees(kappa * L) for both responses.

Physical fabrication and measurement were done. All four specimens printed by multi-material FFF from the generated G-code (repo: Bambu Lab X1 Carbon, 0.4 mm nozzle). Thermal specimens submerged in near-boiling water; hygro specimens oven-dried (repo: about 60 C for 4 h) then submerged in room-temperature water. Deformed geometry measured at equilibrium only.

Quantitative results (Table 3), predicted vs measured mean +/- s.d.: Baseline hygro bend 36.4 deg vs 35.3 +/- 3.1 deg (n=3, 3.0% error); Case I thermal bend 52.0 vs 55.7 +/- 4.2 (n=3, 6.6%); Case II hygro twist 41.3 vs 41.3 +/- 2.2 (n=4, 0.1%); Case III thermal twist 23.0 vs 23.3 +/- 2.5 (n=3, 1.4%). All predictions within one s.d. of the measured mean. 'No case required manual redesign after G-code generation.'

Table 1 process windows for the baseline bilayer: nozzle temp active PA6-GF [260, 290] C nominal 275 C (curvature change < 1%); passive PA612-CF [280, 300] C nominal 290 C (< 1%); print speed active [20, 40] mm/s nominal 30 (< 2%); passive [30, 60] mm/s nominal 45 (< 1%); infill active fixed 1.0; passive [0.8, 1.0] nominal 1.0 (about 8%); layer height [0.1, 0.3] mm nominal 0.3 mm (< 3%); bed 90 C. Layer resolution 0.3 mm gives n1 = 2 passes for h1 = 0.6 mm. The paper does not say how the sensitivity percentages were obtained (model or experiment).

Parameter values are not in the paper; they are in material panels inside ct_design.gh. Extracted by raw-deflate decompression of the file: PA6-GF E=2850 MPa, alpha_L=1.0e-4, alpha_T=5.0e-3 /C, chi_L=5.0e-3, chi_T=1.1e-2; PA612-CF15 E=5140 MPa, alpha_L=3.0e-5, alpha_T=1.0e-4, chi_L=1.2e-3, chi_T=7.0e-3; PLA E=3500 MPa, alpha_L=6.8e-5, alpha_T=1.0e-4; PLA-CF E=6000 MPa, alpha_L=2.0e-5, alpha_T=8.0e-5; biological panels pine_sclerenchyma E=650 MPa, chi_L=0.01, chi_T=0.05; pine_sclereid E=30 MPa, chi_L=0.02, chi_T=0.20; bauhinia E=2000 MPa, chi_L=0.005, chi_T=0.18. The paper calls these 'approximate parameters taken from datasheets and the literature'; no per-value source is given.
The repo holds a 'bauhinia' material panel (a chiral seed pod genus) although the paper reports no seed-pod instantiation; it is unused in the four published cases.

Pipeline defaults in the repo: RH_ref = 30%, RH = 80% (du = 0.5 as a fraction), T_ref = 25 C, T_cur = 80 C, h_1 = h_2 = 0.06 cm, L = 10 cm, W = 1 cm, layer height 0.3 mm, nozzle 0.4 mm, filament 1.75 mm, tolerance epsilon = 0.05. Verification in spec.py passes when |C_geom(spec) - C_geom(art)|/|C_geom(art)| <= epsilon, the same for kappa, and speed and nozzle temperature sit inside each material's window.

The code evaluates the model at equilibrium only (F_fil.py: eps = coefficient * du, report string 'at equilibrium'). The relaxation ODEs of eqs 6, 9, 17 are never integrated and no time constant is in any panel. The dynamic part of 'stimulus-response dynamical systems' is therefore untested; only static end states were predicted and measured.

Own calculation, C_geom from eq 16 with h1 = h2 = 0.06 cm: hygro pair n = 2850/5140 gives C = 12.226 /cm; thermal pair n = 3500/6000 gives C = 12.272 /cm; symmetric n = 1 gives 12.5 /cm (= 1.5/h, matching Lean's bilayerCurvature_symmetric).
findings.source_url_or_path: own calculation from panel values in ct_design.gh and formula in gh_scripts/S_print.py

findings.claim: Reproduction attempt (own calculation, angle = degrees(C * d * L), L = 10 cm). Hygro twist with du = 1.0 (RH 0 to 100%): d_12 = 0.5(5e-3 - 1.1e-2) + 0.5(1.2e-3 - 7e-3) = -5.9e-3, angle = 41.33 deg in magnitude, matching the paper's 41.3. The other three do NOT follow from one obvious setting: hygro bend gives 34.3 deg (90/0, du = 0.5), 68.7 deg (90/0, du = 1.0) or -7.0 deg (0/90 as the paper states, du = 0.5), versus 36.4 predicted (needs du about 0.53 with 90/0); thermal bend 52.0 needs dT about 92 C and thermal twist 23.0 needs dT about 71 C with the PLA/PLA-CF panels. I could not recover the slider settings used for Table 3.
findings.source_url_or_path: own calculation; inputs from ct_design.gh panels and gh_scripts/*.py

findings.claim: Repo/paper inconsistencies observed: (a) hygro_bend.gcode header says mat1 PA6-GF theta = 90, mat2 PA612-CF15 theta = 0, the reverse of the paper's 0/90; (b) its header kappa = 0.0763 /cm implies 43.7 deg over 10 cm, not 36.4; (c) both thermal G-code headers record kappa = 0.0000 /cm; (d) PA6-GF speed window is [20,40] mm/s in paper Table 1, 30-60 in the setup guide, 60-130 in the .gh panel; (e) PA6-GF chi_T is 1.1e-2 in the .gh panel and 1.2e-2 in the setup guide; (f) thermal G-code nozzle temperatures are 208/215 C, bed 55 C.

Twist crosstalk (own analysis). Eq 28 assumes both layers share the same eps_L, eps_T. The printed twist specimens use two different materials, and the code computes d_12 = d12_1 - d12_2 and a separate d_thk labelled 'crosstalk'. With the panel values and du = 1: eps_strip_1 = (5e-3 + 1.1e-2)/2 = 8.0e-3, eps_strip_2 = (1.2e-3 + 7e-3)/2 = 4.1e-3, so d_thk = 3.9e-3 and the same Timoshenko formula predicts a simultaneous bend of degrees(12.226 * 3.9e-3 * 10) = 27.3 deg alongside the 41.3 deg twist. The paper reports only a twist angle and does not discuss the coupled bend.

Stated limitations and future work: deterministic only, to be extended to compositional uncertainty propagation and a probabilistic admissibility through pi; process windows are one-parameter-at-a-time slices, a joint admissible space with parameter coupling is future work; bilayers are 'the minimal nontrivial instantiation', richer geometries, more scales and nonlinear constitutive laws are future work; heterogeneous inputs need the presheaf/sheaf formulation; a single composed case is 'the minimal proof' of generativity; proposed extension to multi-agent or neurosymbolic discovery where 'the simulation condition then acts as a type-level filter... returning rejected candidates to the proposer with an explicit interface failure'.

The paper claims a library of validated laws {F_i} and reductions {beta_j} 'closes combinatorially into |F_i| * |beta_j| candidate actuators, each verified by construction'. Demonstrated size: 2 x 2 = 4, of which one (thermal twist) is the composed case.

Funding and roles: MIT Lemelson Engineering Fellowship, Singapore-DSO, MGAIC. Marom: conceptualization, methodology, software, validation, investigation, writing. Buehler: conceptualization, supervision, funding. Zardini: methodology, review. Tibbits: methodology.

Repo facts: lamm-mit/CategoryTheoryDesign, Apache-2.0, created 2026-04-21, last push 2026-08-02, 32 stars at fetch time. Contents: ct_design.gh (68,640 bytes) and ct_design.3dm, 41 Python scripts in gh_scripts/ (one per object or morphism, plus spec.py, comp.py, viz.py, machine_bambu_x1c.py), four G-code files, four actuation videos (baseline_x60, case1_x15, case2_x60, case3_x15), figures. No tests, no formal proofs, no raw measurement data files (angles per specimen are not in the repo tree).

The repo README documents extension recipes for a new stimulus (light, pH), a new kinematic response (rolling), a new natural system (sunflower heliotropism is the named example), a new substrate or process ('silicone, LCE'; 'DIW, SLA': copy S_print.py and replace the bilayer expression) and a new printer (new machine_*.py profile feeding the same comp.py). A resin (SLA) machine profile does not exist in the repo.

MRS Bulletin paper: Marom and Buehler, 'Frontiers of biological material intelligence', MRS Bulletin 50(12), 1492-1504, published online 2025-11-26, doi:10.1557/s43577-025-00987-8, CC-BY 4.0, 123 references, cited 7 times per Crossref at fetch. It is a review/perspective with no new equations, parameters or experiments. It defines material intelligence as the capacity to 'sense, respond, adapt, and self-optimize' and organizes it into three design principles: sensing and responding to stimuli; self-optimization and feedback loops; encoding history and learning from past states.

MRS Bulletin content relevant to this project: one paragraph on category theory and ologs as a route to transferable design strategies; a fabrication section that names SLA, DLP and two-photon polymerization as the high-resolution route for responsive systems and FFF/DIW for material-specific control; stated bottlenecks are limited material palettes, slow and costly lithography printing at scale, and biofabrication sterility; future directions name optogenetically controlled gene circuits and closed loops between computational prediction, physical realization and refinement. The flytrap appears as an example of memory (two touches within a time window).

Lee Marom's other publications found: (1) arXiv:2603.14312, 'Autonomous Agents Coordinating Distributed Discovery Through Emergent Artifact Exchange', F. Y. Wang, L. Marom, S. Pal, R. K. Luu, W. Lu, J. A. Berkovich, M. J. Buehler, 2026-03-15; (2) the MRS Bulletin review; (3) the JMPS paper. The arXiv author search returned exactly two entries; a Crossref author query (from 2018) returned only the MRS item under the exact name.

Lean, machine-checked and matching the paper: StimulusResponseSystem (X, E, f) and StimulusResponseHom with the simulation condition fderiv alpha x (f x e) = g (alpha x) (alphaE e) (paper eq 4); identity; comp_simulation (closure under composition by chain rule, the paper's Proposition A.2); id_comp, comp_id, comp_assoc; a Mathlib CategoryTheory.Category instance (stimulusResponseCategory). No 'sorry' appears in the file. I did not rebuild it in this run.

Lean differs from the paper's Dyn in three ways: X is a real normed vector space rather than a finite-dimensional smooth manifold (so f : X -> E -> X, no tangent bundle); E is a bare Type with no structure and alphaE is an arbitrary function (paper: smooth manifold, smooth map); alpha is only Differentiable, and f carries no regularity at all (paper: smooth). The Lean category is therefore a different, larger category than the paper's Dyn, restricted to flat state spaces.

Lean goes beyond the paper in two places: mapsSolutions proves a morphism carries any solution curve of x' = f(x, e(t)) to a solution of y' = g(y, alphaE(e(t))), which the paper asserts only in words ('the map commutes with time evolution'); and bilayerCurvature_ofEquilibrium derives the Timoshenko coefficient from force balance, moment balance and interface strain compatibility of a two-layer Euler-Bernoulli strip, where the paper only cites Timoshenko 1925.

Lean, machine-checked mechanics that match paper equations: timoshenkoCoefficient is paper eq 16 verbatim; bilayerCurvature is eq 15; linearity, zero, sign and the symmetric case kappa = (3/2) Delta_eps / h; axialStrain is eq 13; shearStrain is the eps_12 formula of Case II; shearStrain_mismatch is eq 28; axialStrain_mismatch = 0 formalizes 'drives a twist rather than a bend'; strainInStripAxes_entries derives both formulas from the rank-2 rotation R diag(eps_L, eps_T) R^T, which the paper does not show.

In the Lean file but NOT in this paper: the diffusive time h^2/D and slowest heat-equation mode (hygromorph-response-time), the flytrap snap parameter alpha = L^4 kappa^2 / h^2 with its monotonicity lemmas, and the poroelastic time mu L^2/(k E). The paper gives no h^2/D scaling and no flytrap equation; these presumably come from the paper's references 25 and 15 (Reyssat and Mahadevan 2009; Forterre et al. 2005), which I verified exist but did not read in this run.

Paper statements NOT machine-checked in Hygromorphs.lean: Nat and Art as full subcategories; Proposition A.4 (compatible reduction induces unique dynamics); the fiber relaxation law eq 6 as an object and alpha_1 (averaging) as a morphism to eq 9; the product object for tissue (eq 12); alpha_geom as a morphism with geometry adjoined at zero dynamics (A.20-A.25) and the element law eq 17; theta = L kappa and alpha_3 as a morphism; the thermal eigenstrain law and eq 29; any twist-curvature formula; the functor F and its functoriality (A.39-A.44); the natural transformation eta and A.53; Spec, Comp, pi, E and their functoriality; the process-window definition eq 25; every numerical result. The file's header says its claims come from claim-sources/plant-hygromorph-mechanics/claims/key-claims.json; that folder is not present in the local leanbio checkout, so I could not compare claim ids.

recommendations: Correct the project's working description of this paper before citing it: it formalizes the pine cone only. Awns, seed pods, flytrap and nacre are motivation. Citing it for flytrap or awn mechanics would be wrong; cite the primary sources (Forterre 2005, Elbaum 2007, Armon 2011) for those.

What the authors would most want from a Lean-verified printed demonstration (my inference from their stated future work): (1) their Appendix A turned from prose into machine-checked statements, especially the functor F with a non-identity iota for a concrete material substitution, the reduction proposition A.4, and the naturality square A.53; (2) the 'simulation condition as a type-level filter that returns rejected candidates with an explicit interface failure' made real, i.e. a checker that REJECTS an ill-typed composition; the paper shows only four successes and no rejection; (3) a new machine backend proving the 'different compilation functors on the same Spec' claim, which today has exactly one instance (Bambu X1C FFF).

A resin (SLA) demonstration is a genuine extension, not a restatement: the repo names 'SLA' and a new S_<process>.py as the extension path but has not built it, and the MRS Bulletin review singles out SLA/DLP as the high-resolution route. It requires a new Spec instantiation (exposure, layer, orientation and post-cure instead of raster angle and bead width), because vat-photopolymer parts lack raster anisotropy, so the mismatch must come from material pairing, cure gradient or geometry rather than from phi. That forces a new tissue-level object and reduction and is the scientifically interesting part.

Novelty lever 1, dynamics: the paper's objects are dynamical but only static equilibrium angles were predicted and measured, and no relaxation time appears anywhere. Hygromorphs.lean already has the diffusive h^2/D time and slowest-mode decay. A joint paper that predicts and measures actuation TIME versus thickness (tau proportional to h^2, a 2x thickness giving 4x time) on printed strips would test the part of Dyn the original paper leaves untested, using theorems already proved.

Novelty lever 2, a derived morphism the paper lacks: prove in Lean that the fiber relaxation law composed with averaging, stacking, the Timoshenko map and theta = L kappa is a morphism end to end, and state exactly which hypotheses are needed (for example, alpha_1 averaging is a morphism only when the relaxation law is affine in the state and fibers share tau; the paper assumes the uniform case). Machine-checking will surface these side conditions; reporting them is a contribution.

Novelty lever 3, the two-material twist: eq 28 and Lean's shearStrain_mismatch assume one material at +/-phi, but the printed specimens use two. Formalize the general two-material +/-phi bilayer, show the axial mismatch is (eps_strip_1 - eps_strip_2) and non-zero, and predict the coupled bend. My estimate from the repo's own panels is about 27 deg of bend alongside the 41 deg twist at full hygro stimulus. Check this against the authors' videos before asserting it publicly; if it holds, it is a concrete case where formalization finds something the informal treatment passed over.

Novelty lever 4, a failing composition: design one candidate that the simulation condition or an interface type rejects (for example a reduction that is not closed under the dynamics per A.15) and one bistable snap element (the Lean file already has the L^4 kappa^2 / h^2 parameter) where the linear Timoshenko chain is provably the wrong element model. Showing the framework says 'no' is what would make a 'verified by construction' claim credible to a mechanics audience.

Before building on the published numbers, ask the authors for the slider settings (RH_ref, RH, T_ref, T_cur) behind Table 3 and for per-specimen angle data. I could reproduce only the hygro-twist prediction from the public files, and the G-code headers disagree with the paper on raster order and curvature.

State the Lean/paper gap honestly in any joint text: the Lean category uses normed vector spaces, bare-Type stimuli and mere differentiability, so it is not literally the paper's Dyn. Either generalize to manifolds (Mathlib has smooth manifolds and mfderiv) or say plainly that the checked statement is the flat-space case, which covers every example in the paper since all state spaces there are subsets of R^n.

Treat n = 3 to 4 specimens and 'within one s.d.' as modest evidence. A joint paper should pre-register the predicted angle and time before printing, and report all specimens, which fits this project's freeze-then-test protocol.

specialists.topic: Mamou-Mani Architects and Fab.Pub: what they build, with what, and where the material gaps are
specialists.summary: Mamou-Mani (London, Arthur Mamou-Mani) describes itself as 'Computational architecture, circular design and digital fabrication'; its fabrication company is Fab Pub Ltd (Fab.Pub, 22 Gossamer Gardens, London E2), which runs robotic large-format pellet/filament extrusion and laser cutting. Fetched project pages show two material families: (a) 3D-printed PLA bioplastic modules (Conifera 2019, 700 modules; Aurora 2021; Altostrata 2023, 12 modules, 30 m long; The Wavery 2023; The Roe 2023-24, thirty ~20 kg modules) and (b) timber, plywood, rattan, zinc, sand and ceramic (Temple Galaxia 2018; Miami Waves 2018; Sandwaves 2020; Smile 2021; THK Tower 2021-24; Hermes Sanlitun facade 2024-26). The software pipeline named in sources is parametric design in Rhino/Grasshopper with the open-source Silkworm G-code plugin (Holloway, Mamou-Mani, Kjelstrup-Johnson) and, for Aurora, Dassault Systemes 3DEXPERIENCE / xGenerative Design. Stated material limits, all from the practice's own words: PLA only composts industrially (60 C, 100% humidity, about one month); 'there is a contradiction between the idea of sustainable or durable and biodegradable'; PLA is 'not very well researched compared to Pet-based polymers'; it costs more than petroleum plastic; interior PLA must be 'compounded with fireproof materials'. Their carbon-saving figure for PLA is inconsistent across sources (68%, 80%, and 73.7% computed from their own Aurora LCA numbers). Five gaps follow: programmable end-of-life, heat/weather durability outdoors, intrinsic fire performance, a verified structural property envelope with less mass, and passive stimulus-responsive skins. A credible proof of concept is a hand-scale (about 100-200 mm) family of 3-6 interlocking, reversible-joint modules with a translucent or wood-filled finish, delivered with a Grasshopper definition and a one-page measured datasheet. Not found: any direct statement by the practice on UV, creep or moisture; any fire test class; printer models or build volumes; the RIBA/Westminster research folio (HTTP 403).

Altostrata structural evidence is a single in-house test with ARUP and Fab Pub reporting resistance to pull forces of '500 kg.m2' (unit as printed on the page; it is not a valid force or pressure unit, so the figure cannot be interpreted without the test report)
The practice itself says PLA is 'not very well researched compared to Pet-based polymers' and that bioplastics are generally assumed weaker than petroleum polymers
Fab.Pub is described as a joint venture between Mamou-Mani Architects and Therme Group

Aurora (2021, Design Museum London, for Dassault Systemes) is 3D-printed bio-sourced PLA modules hung on steel tubes, 'printed, broken down and re-printed on site', designed on the 3DEXPERIENCE platform; LCA (EF 3.0) gives 2333.89 kgCO2 for PLA vs 8890.42 kgCO2 for an ABS version

The practice's PLA carbon claim is inconsistent across its own statements: '68 per cent more carbon efficient' (Dezeen 2019), 'PLA uses 80% less carbon' (Therme 2024, citing an ARUP report it commissioned), 'up to 80% lower carbon emissions than ABS' (Fab.Pub), and 73.7% from the Aurora LCA numbers
Mamou-Mani stated PLA must go to an industrial composter at 60 C and 100% humidity, taking about one month; a home composter takes about six months
findings.value: 60 C; 100% humidity; ~1 month industrial; ~6 months home

findings.claim: Mamou-Mani named the core tension himself: 'there is a contradiction between the idea of sustainable or durable and biodegradable, which is the opposite'; he calls PLA 'a nice middle ground' that must be activated in an industrial composter; Fab.Pub runs a take-back scheme (crush to pellets, reprint)

In a 6 March 2024 interview he said PLA 'remains more expensive than petroleum plastics', 'People have said that it's worse than petroleum plastics in terms of usability', 'We're still doing studies to find out more'; wishes include PLA from British sugar beet, restaurant waste or crayfish feedstock, and 'a city that looks like nature'

Design philosophy in his words: 'Designs emerge from the constraints of reality rather than through ego-led geometry'; 'with parametric design you bring the shapes in from the bottom up, guided by parameters'; architect as 'a gardener ... growing beautiful, natural things, and evolving them'

The Roe (Canary Wharf, Jan 2023 - Feb 2024): central tree 6.4 m wide x 4.0 m tall from thirty 3D-printed modules 'in PLA bioplastics, compounded with fireproof materials for interior use'; each module about 20 kg and 15-20 hours to print on a robotic arm; internal CNC-cut plywood support; 42 m bar clad in printed backlit modules

findings.claim: The Wavery (2023, Fortnum & Mason, London): bar, ceiling elements and stools 3D printed in PLA bioplastic at Fab.Pub's London workshop

findings.value: 85,000 m2; 240 x 80 x 60 m; 50% steel reduction (claimed)

findings.claim: Fab.Pub material palette: Clear PLA, Wood PLA (recycled wood dust), Paper PLA (cellulose fibre), Recycled White PLA, terracotta, stoneware, plywood, natural fabric, cardboard; custom blends with 'coffee, oyster shells and other materials' designed with 'performance, fire safety, and regulatory compliance in mind'; no named fire class or test result on the page

Fab.Pub offers robotic large-format 3D printing 'for furniture, interiors, installations and architectural components', a container 'Mobile Factory', 'Custom material development, take-back and selected waste-stream R&D'; minimum project budget GBP 250 and minimum 2 weeks; customer-supplied material must be confirmed suitable first

Silkworm is a plugin that translates Grasshopper/Rhino geometry into G-code, by Adam Holloway, Arthur Mamou-Mani and Karl Kjelstrup-Johnson, released open source; Mamou-Mani: 'Silkworm is a plug-in that translates geometric designs into g-code which informs the 3D printers'. Authorship and Grasshopper link come from search-result summaries (food4rhino returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch); the quote is from the fetched Therme interview
Mamou-Mani and Toby Burgess published a peer-reviewed-journal article on digitally fabricated, crowdfunded student pavilions (Architectural Design 85:130-135, 2015)

Independent literature: 3D-printed PLA has a glass transition of 65 C (DMTA); modulus drops from 1045.7 MPa (glassy) to 1.2 MPa (rubbery); compressive yield falls from 110 MPa (room temp, 0.1 /s) to 42 MPa (50 C, 0.0001 /s)
findings.value: Tg 65 C; own calculation: 42/110 = 38% of room-temperature yield retained at 50 C and slow loading

findings.claim: Independent literature: PLA lattice properties 'degrade due to environmental factors' (room temperature, humidity, natural light); loss of failure strain matters more than loss of yield stress for impact; gradient auxetic cores kept ~800 N peak force and up to 40% more energy absorption at moderate degradation

Independent literature: 4D-printed cellulosic hygromorphic bilayers were run as weather-responsive facade shading for over a year and deployed on a real building facade, with no external energy; and 3D-printed wood-filled composites can be programmed to self-transform with humidity

GAP 1 - programmable end of life. They want durable-in-use yet biodegradable and call that a contradiction; PLA only breaks down at 60 C / 100% humidity in an industrial facility. A stimulus-triggered material (stable in service, degradation switched on by a defined trigger) answers their own stated problem

GAP 2 - heat and weather durability outdoors. They show PLA pavilions in hot climates (Singapore, Dubai) and offer only temporary/touring PLA structures, while their permanent outdoor works use timber, rattan, ceramic and metal; literature puts PLA Tg at 65 C with large strength loss by 50 C and property loss under humidity and light. No UV, creep or moisture statement from the practice was found

GAP 3 - intrinsic fire performance. Interior PLA is 'compounded with fireproof materials for interior use' and custom blends are designed around 'fire safety, and regulatory compliance', so fire is handled by additives per project; no fire class is published. A bio-based formulation with built-in char/fire behaviour that still recycles through their crush-and-reprint loop is unmet

GAP 4 - verified property envelope and less mass. They say PLA is 'not very well researched', rely on one in-house pull test with an uninterpretable unit, and print heavy solid-walled modules (~20 kg and 15-20 h each at The Roe; ~5 kg each at Conifera by calculation). A law-constrained hierarchical lattice with machine-checked scaling bounds and a measured datasheet would cut mass and print time and give engineers numbers

GAP 5 - passive stimulus response. Their environmental skins are static (Hermes ceramic sun filter; rattan that only changes colour) or motorised (Flying Whales textile doors). Humidity-driven self-shaping printed bilayers have been demonstrated at facade scale by others but do not appear in any fetched Mamou-Mani or Fab.Pub page

Proof-of-concept that would read as credible to them (my proposal, inferred from their module language, not a statement by the practice): 3-6 interlocking modules of about 100-200 mm each, square-motif or wave geometry, reversible dry or cable-tie joints, translucent or wood-filled finish that takes backlighting, one measurable behaviour predicted in advance (e.g. humidity-driven aperture opening angle, or stiffness per gram of a graded lattice vs a solid wall), supplied with the Grasshopper definition and a one-page datasheet. Their own smallest job is a GBP 250, 2-week order and their range runs down to '300 small figurines'

Process mismatch to flag (unverified background, not fetched in this run): Fab.Pub's production route is thermoplastic pellet/filament extrusion on robots, whereas Formlabs machines are resin (SLA) and powder (SLS) printers. A Formlabs print can show geometry and a responsive mechanism but will not by itself show that the material runs on Fab.Pub's extruders or re-pelletises in their take-back loop

recommendations: Lead the pitch with their own sentence: 'there is a contradiction between the idea of sustainable or durable and biodegradable'. Frame the new material as resolving that contradiction with a defined trigger, since it is the one limitation the founder has stated on record.

Design the proof of concept as a module family, not a single object: 3-6 interlocking pieces about 100-200 mm, reversible joints, translucent or wood-filled finish, one behaviour predicted before printing and then measured. Ship the Grasshopper definition with it so it drops into their Silkworm/Grasshopper workflow.

Pick ONE of the five gaps for the first object. Passive humidity response (gap 5) or mass reduction through a graded lattice (gap 4) can be shown at desk scale; fire (gap 3) and outdoor durability (gap 2) need test-lab evidence a small print cannot supply.

State the process mismatch up front: a resin or powder print shows geometry and mechanism only. Offer a second step in which the same geometry is run on Fab.Pub's pellet extruder in Wood PLA or Paper PLA, which their site says needs material suitability sign-off and a GBP 250 / 2-week minimum.

Bring a one-page datasheet with units and test method. Their own published evidence is one pull test with an unusable unit and three different carbon percentages, so numbers with provenance are a point of difference.

Ask them directly for what was not found here: fire classification achieved on The Roe modules, any creep/UV/moisture data from the touring Altostrata, extruder nozzle and build envelope, and whether the Wood PLA or cellulose-filled PLA shows humidity movement they currently treat as a defect.
Do not repeat their carbon percentages in the paper or dashboard as fact; cite the Aurora LCA figures (2333.89 vs 8890.42 kgCO2) with the computed 73.7% and note it comes from the software partner.

specialists.topic: Chemistry: which printable photopolymers and powders swell in water, and by how much (Formlabs SLA resins, PA11/PA12/TPU SLS powders, open-mode hydrogel resins)
specialists.summary: Stock Formlabs materials barely swell in water. On Formlabs' own 24 h immersion table (1 cm cubes) every current SLA resin gains under 1% mass in water (Rigid 10K <0.1%, Tough 2000 V2 0.19%, Flexible 80A 0.7%, Elastic 50A V2 0.7%, Clear V5 0.9%), and the SLS materials gain 0.1% (Nylon 11, Nylon 12) to 0.9% (TPU 90A). Dense PA12 and PA11 saturate at 1.6% and 1.9% by immersion (Arkema, ISO 62). I found no measured hygroscopic expansion coefficient for any Formlabs resin or for PA11/PA12, and no water diffusion coefficient for any Formlabs resin; the strains below are my estimates from mass uptake, calibrated on a measured polyamide 6.6 coefficient. Best stock pair on one Formlabs SLA printer: Clear/Grey V5 (active) bonded to Rigid 10K (passive), estimated differential linear strain about 0.2% after 24 h, rising to roughly 0.7-0.9% after a week (Grey V5 tensile bars gained 3.2% mass in one week of DI water and kept about 65% of dry modulus; that row mapping is my reading of a scrambled PDF table). That is enough to bend a thin strip visibly, but it is slow and small. PA12 on the Fuse gives about 0.2-0.45% from dry to saturated, with no good passive partner in the same build. The largest realistic differential comes from leaving stock resins: a PEG-acrylate hydrogel resin in Open Material Mode (Form 3/4, 405 nm) against a stock or TPGDA-type passive layer. Measured linear swelling of printed PEG-acrylate resins is 3.5% (neat PEGDA 250), 19.3% (PEGDA 575 + PEGMEMA) and 74.1% (PEGMEMA-based), against <0.5% for TPGDA (Maennel 2020, printed on an Asiga DLP at 385 nm, not on a Formlabs machine). I found no paper that printed a hydrogel on a Formlabs printer. Caution for anyone reusing the Formlabs table: an automated summary of that page shifted the columns and reported 163.9% water gain for Elastic 50A V2; my direct parse of the HTML shows 163.9% is the xylene column and water is 0.7%.
